div.p: The fundamental target of real-time scheduling is to execute the task set, such that their deadlines are never missed. The major concern in safety-critical and mixed criticality real-time systems is that correct output should be generated before deadline even in the presence of faults. With the advent of low cost COTS there is rise in the transient faults. This lay off can be met by using fault tolerant techniques to make the system reliable. The empirical evaluation and simulation of partitioned and global approaches of scheduling for the avionics task set gives an insight of issues in achieving reliability.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: A mixed criticality is a system which can execute various applications of different criticality such as safety critical, non-safety critical and different critical levels. The cyber physical systems, Internet of things, automotive and avionics are examples of mixed critical systems. In view of increment in air traffic and propelled computerization, Air traffic control (ATC) is among the most requesting of all product applications. Air traffic control system is a hard real time system, the deadlines must be strictly met; it is safety critical. The results can be catastrophic if the system does not perform accurately. Many of the controllers work together to guide the aircraft in the airspace. Air traffic controllers do the various tasks, from issue landing, and take off instructions to the pilot to monitoring and directing the aircraft movement on the ground and in the air. It also provides consultive aid to aircraft in non-controlled airspace.

The tasks of the air traffic control system run on multicore embedded processor system.at various critical levels. Also, these tasks should ensure safety, stability and reliability. All the safety critical systems should guarantee real-time performance and also make effective use of the available processing capacity. This effective usage of processing capabilities in multicore systems and for real time performance, efficient scheduling policies or algorithms are required. The real time scheduling algorithms are supported by accurate schedulability analysis techniques. Hence, fault tolerance at scheduling real time systems needs attention [1][2][3][4][5]. In this paper review of fault tolerant scheduling algorithm in multicore real time systems is summarized in section II. Section III details the system model considered in the analysis and section IV gives the experimentation details for an avionics case study. The task model with three criticality levels has been considered for the analysis.

div.head: II. REVIEW OF FAULT TOLERANT TASK SCHEDULING TECHNIQUES
div.p: One of the major troubles in the design of safety systems is commitment of correct results before the task deadline even in the presence of transient faults. The exploration of various papers is done to understand fault tolerant scheduling in mixed critical systems and various techniques used in achieving reliability or to make the system fault tolerant has been studied.

Scheduling of task mix with variant criticality on a uniprocessor system in the presence of transient faults has been studied. Fault tolerant scheduling algorithm for mixedcriticality systems using re-execution technique for fault tolerance is proposed. Extensive simulations are done to improve the system reliability and schedule feasibility. Only two critical levels for task safety are considered. Multicore Platforms with more levels of criticality can be considered as a future scope [6]. The scheduling policy as proposed by Anand Bhat et.al communicates with tasks to execute simultaneously on various cores in multicore system. The technique used allocates the execution of replicas in time to achieve small response times. Once the fault occurs, the recovery time for a given task in fault tolerant systems depends on many factors. The recovery time of the task is influenced by task allocation, task priorities of both the original and replicated task, current load of the system and the scheduling policy. The recovery time requirement of each task can vary with task and application. For example, in automated driving systems, tasks like perception and steering control have sensitive recovery time as they are highly critical tasks. The recovery time can be flexible in case of tasks like heating control and mission planning. Rate-Monotonic Scheduling is used for recovery time analysis of software tasks in a real-time system. The timing analysis for the task model is done for single error model, which can be enhanced for multiple errors [4]. A cross layer solution, consisting of hardware support and with replicated software re-execution has been done to achieve reliability in mixed real time systems. A replica aware co-scheduling is proposed for mixed criticality systems which improves the schedulability of the system [5]. Resilient scheduling strategies for mixed-criticality systems are proposed by Barauh et.al. Control Theoretic approach is used to manage the budget needed for allocation. The main approach used here to achieve resiliency is reduce the priorities of the LO critical tasks, increase the period and deadline of LO critical tasks and abandon LO critical tasks in a particular pattern. Scheduling strategy uses two servers, one each for servicing the hi-criticality and lo-criticality workloads. Number of criticality levels can be increased and a multicore architecture can be used for running the servers [2]. A Fault-Tolerant Multicore (FTM) scheduling algorithm is proposed based on redundant execution of backups to mask the errors and tolerate core failures. Global scheduling is used for scheduling, the primary and backups are not assigned to any core. The primary and the backups are issued on any free core even after pre-emption, for execution [12]. Fault tolerant task allocation strategy has been proposed by Anand et.al. The task allocation is always done on a core which does not have the primary backup of the task. Simulated annealing has been applied to fault tolerant allocation for analysis of recovery time of each task [4]. To maintain levels of reliability probabilistic modelling of task scheduling has been studied for Network On-Chip based platforms. Both single and multiple errors are considered during reliability evaluation. Clustered replication method is used to reduce the communications between the cores in multicore systems. This also reduces execution latency of graph representation of the tasks. The tasks are clustered based on the number of instances [13].

div.head: SUMMARY OF REVIEW
div.p: Complex real-time systems like, automobiles with advanced driving-assist features and flight management in avionics must employ redundancy for crucial software tasks to tolerate crash faults. From the survey it is relevant that for resiliency or to achieve reliability different techniques used are replication, primary backup, re-execution of the failed task and clustered replication of the tasks. Fault tolerance techniques have been applied to both global scheduling and partitioned scheduling. Also, almost all the literature considers only two critical levels, whereas complex real time systems can have tasks at different critical levels. As quoted by Burns et.al in [15] all the automobile and avionics systems have five critical levels. But schedulability analysis of fault tolerant algorithms on multicore systems with different criticality levels needs attention. Some of the approaches used to achieve resiliency and improve schedulability are task dropping of low critical tasks, task stretching of low criticality tasks and reduce priorities of the low critical tasks. The approach of task dropping is also being used on a single processor system. Much of the existing research in mixed critical systems has been done with a single scheduling scheme for all critical levels.

div.head: III. SYSTEM MODEL
div.p: This section highlights the nomenclature used in multicore scheduling research. It also highlights the environment used in the timing analysis of the scheduling approaches.

div.head: A. Types Of Multicore Systems
div.p: In the context of scheduling, multicore systems can be classified into three categories, heterogeneous, homogeneous and uniform. Homogeneous multicores with four cores, has been used for schedulability analysis. In homogeneous multicore systems, the processors are identical and so the rate of execution of all the tasks is not going to vary based on the processor.

div.head: B. Task Model Used for Analysis
div.p: The main objective of the scheduling algorithms in real time systems is to execute the set of tasks, on the system, such that deadlines are not violated. An application comprises of a set of tasks. The task model can be periodic or aperiodic. A task model comprising of both periodic and sporadic tasks has been considered throughout the study where, each task τi is characterized by: its relative deadline Di, worst-case execution time Ci , and minimum inter-arrival time or period Ti for periodic tasks. Tasks are assumed to have implicit deadlines. The utilization ui, of task τi is given by Ti /Ci. The utilization U sum of a taskset is the sum of the utilizations of all of its tasks. H( τ ) is the hyper period of a taskset.

A task set consists of n independent periodic real-time tasks {τ1, τ2 , τ3… τn}. The characteristics of every task τi (1 ≤ i ≤ n) is described by as {Ti, Di, Ni , Li, Ci}, where Ti is the period of the task, Di is the relative deadline, Ni is the maximum number of transient faults that can be tolerated during the task execution, Li Ɛ {Low, Mid, High, Non} is the task criticality level, and Ci is the task worst-case execution time (WCET). In particular, Ci(Low) , Ci(mid) and Ci(High) represent the Worst Case Execution time of task τi in low, medium and high-criticality modes, respectively. div.p: Different types of faults that can occur in mixed critical systems are permanent faults due to failure of processor or transient faults which occur due to event upsets. Transient faults occur for a short time and do not cause any damage to the device. In safety critical embedded systems it is crucial to execute the tasks in the presence of transient faults. Transient faults generally follow exponential distribution with average arrival rate λ, which represents the expected number of failures occurring per second [6]. The probability of successful execution of a task with no transient faults, is given by exponential failure law. Re-execution of the replica can be used to overcome transient faults. The replica can be maintained using triple Modular redundancy as stated by Burns in [15].

div.head: C. Feasibility of Taskset
div.p: Multicore scheduling ventures to solve two things, assignment of the task and setting priorities to the tasks. Scheduling algorithms for multiprocessor systems can be classified based on the priority assignment and allocation. Real time scheduling algorithms are broadly classified into global and partitioned scheduling. Scheduling algorithms that do not allow migration from processor to processor are referred to as partitioned, those where migration is permitted are called as global scheduling. Partitioned scheduling algorithms are not work-conserving, as a processor may become idle, due to the constraint of no migration.

If some scheduling algorithm can schedule all possible sequences of the taskset generated without missing deadlines, than the taskset is said to be feasible and the algorithm is said to be optimal with respect to the task model. Hence a system is guaranteed un-feasible if U >1, but if U < 1 does not guarantee feasibility of the system. U < = Urm (n) in all rate monotonic systems guarantees the feasibility of the system along with utilization of the system to be less than one.

div.head: IV EXPERIMENTATION AND RESULTS
div.p: Cyber physical systems which are controlled and monitored by computer based algorithms fall into the category of mixed critical systems. The example of Avionics control system has been considered in the experimentation and evaluation of partitioned and global scheduling approaches for the system. The air traffic control system comprises of different tasks like take-off and landing instructions, control ground traffic like baggage vehicles and airport workers, display controls about weather updates and other critical information, monitoring aircraft on ground and in air and manage communication with traffic control system. Air traffic control system is safety critical with multiple criticality levels. All these tasks are at different critical levels. The tasks and their critical levels along with task parameters like type, WCET and deadline, are given in table 4.1. The task set pertaining to an air traffic control system comprises of seven different tasks at different critical levels. Three different critical levels are identified for simplicity like high, low and mid instead of five as stated by Burns et.al [15]. The worst-case response time R i of a task helps in schedulability analysis.

div.head: B. Re-execution of highly critical tasks on homogeneous
div.p: Multicore system To achieve fault tolerance, it is assumed that the single fault occurs at the end of task execution. The movement a fault occurs task has to be re-executed. Every task in the task set is associated with criticality levels. In the process of re-execution of task 1, task 7 miss its deadlines on a single processor system. The process of task dropping can be used to improve schedulability as indicated by Pathan and et.al in [12]. But, on a multicore system all the tasks are able to meet the deadlines for a given task set. On a multicore system, an avionics task set comprising of more than 50% high critical tasks is considered to check if task dropping is essential in a multicore system. Task dropping approach can be followed to improve schedulability of the task set on a uniprocessor system. In the example under consideration the avionics task set will be schedulable if the tasks with low and medium critical levels (T2, T4, T6) are dropped. The medium critical task T2 in the task set is monitoring the weather conditions and report the weather critical information. Dropping such tasks can lead to catastrophic conditions. Re-execution of the task is essential for reliability, at max the low critical task can be suspended to avoid deadline miss. The other option is budget reservation to improve schedulability. Every task can have its own budget and if task utilizes the budget beyond the allotted one, than the low critical task can be suspended. These two cases of task suspension and budget reservation form the future direction of study.

div.head: C. Response time analysis in a homogeneous Multicore
div.p: system with task re-execution With single transient fault occurring at the end of one of the critical tasks at least once, the task set is still schedulable on a quad core system using RMFF, P-EDF and G-EDF. The response time analysis for the avionics task set is shown in Figure 4.1. The simulation results indicate that PEDF approach is an appropriate approach for maintaining backups for re-execution, amongst the three variants, as it follows an optimal bin packing strategy to pack the tasks. The Gantt chart for partitioned EDF is shown in figure 4.2. From the Gantt chart it is clear that with partitioned approach, the avionics task set comprising of independent periodic tasks and sporadic tasks, is schedulable with only two cores. Due to which the remaining cores in the multicore system can be used to maintain the replica of the tasks to be used during the faults. It is always better to save a backup copy on a different core to achieve fault tolerance in case of failure. The reliability of the each task is calculated using equation 2. Figure 4.3 shows the reliability of each task against the utilization. The graph indicates reliability of 1 can be achieved for high critical tasks following a triple redundancy model.

div.head: IV. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE DIRECTION
div.p: Mixed critical real-time systems like modern automobiles with advanced driving-assist features and avionics application, once a fault occurs, task has to be re-executed to achieve reliability. It must employ redundancy for crucial software tasks to tolerate permanent crash faults and transient task faults. This redundancy can be achieved by using techniques like active replication or the primary-backup approach. But schedulability analysis of fault tolerant algorithms on multicore systems with different criticality levels needs attention. The simulation results also indicate that approach of dropping a low criticality task on a single core system improves the schedulability of the task set whereas in a multicore system task dropping may not be essential. This leads to an interesting future analysis whether all the backups of a task should be executed or a task dropping of low critical task is essential in a multicore real time system.
